subject: Re: Standalone appliance image revocation and dispatch plan
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, ciso@atlashealth.com, procurement@atlashealth.com, ops@shipsafe.io
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Standalone appliance image revocation and dispatch plan

Team and Atlas stakeholders —

Following our call this morning, I’m putting the proposed revocation + dispatch workflow here for review. This is aimed at AtlasHealth’s standalone appliances (air-gapped customers) where we must be able to: 1) revoke a signed image quickly, 2) provide a signed replacement bundle, and 3) evidence the chain-of-custody during the physical media handoff.

Key constraints:
- Customer operates in a locked room; only ShipSafe handles transit.
- No internet connectivity at target site.
- Atlas requires proof-of-signing and a revocation list signed by Redwood KMS.

Proposed high-level steps:
1) Build and sign image (appliance-image-v3.2). Signatures: code-sig + signature of manifest by signing-keyring-20270110.pem.
2) Generate revocation-list-20270112.json if image must be revoked; sign it and timestamp via HSM.
3) Create a small USB media with: signed image signature file, signed manifest, human-readable checklist, and chain-of-custody barcode. Seal in tamper-evident envelope.
4) ShipSafe picks up from Redwood staging and performs two-person verification; generates pickup receipt and scans barcode into the drive link above.
5) On arrival, Atlas onsite engineer verifies seals and signature using the public key we published to their secure vault.
6) If revocation occurs after shipment but before install, we will: issue revocation-list (signed), notify Atlas CISO and ShipSafe with urgent pickup request, and prepare replacement bundle with expedited courier.

Questions for the group:
- Karthik: can you confirm the HSM stamping time format and the minimum TTL we should publish on revocation lists?
- Marissa: is the ShipSafe SLA sufficient for a 24-hour urgent pickup in us-west?
- Mina: what evidence package should we include for SOC2/audit (logs, signed timestamps, manifest)?

Attachments: signed-keyring-20270110.pem (public key), draft manifest (attached below as a sig reference).

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, ciso@atlashealth.com, ops@shipsafe.io
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Standalone appliance image revocation and dispatch plan

Lauren —

Thanks for drafting. A few specifics from the infra side:
- HSM stamping: we will embed an RFC3161 timestamp and HSM signature. That produces a time format compatible with the customer vault verification. TTL: recommend we publish revocation lists with a 7-day window by default and allow emergency 0-day revokes (marked high-priority).
- Revocation distribution: revocation-list-20270112.json should include fields: image_id, build_hash, revoked_at (RFC3339), reason, hsm_signature. I attached a sample revocation-list-20270112.json (signature included).
- Key rotation: public-key publication cadence — we should push an updated public key to Atlas' vault and record the key_id in the manifest.
- On-device verification: offline verification script will check signature chain against known key_ids; we will provide Atlas a small verification binary and a checksum.

Operational notes:
- ShipSafe confirmed normal SLA is 72 hours for non-urgent pickups; they can scope in a 24-hour expedited option at 2x cost (ops@shipsafe.io confirmed on call).
- For evidence: include the build log snapshot, HSM timestamp proof, manifest, and the signed receipt from ShipSafe scan. Mina — I’d recommend we encrypt the build log and place it in the Drive link; Atlas auditors should have access to the decryption key via their KMS.

I attached: revocation-list-20270112.json (signed) and appliance-image-v3.2.tar.gz.sig (signature only).

-karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: AtlasHealth CISO <ciso@atlashealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com, ops@shipsafe.io
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Standalone appliance image revocation and dispatch plan

Hello Lauren / Redwood team —

Appreciate the thorough plan. A couple of audit/security clarifications before we sign off on the on-site acceptance flow:
1) Chain-of-custody proof: we need a signed pickup manifest from ShipSafe that includes GPS coordinates at pickup and delivery scan times. Can ShipSafe add these fields?
2) Revocation notice consumption: If a revocation happens after the media is already at our site, what is the on-demand verification/kill switch we must run locally to ensure the image is rejected if revoked? We need a simple SOP for our engineers (2-3 commands maximum) and an on-call Redwood contact.
3) Key compromise scenario: If Redwood suspects private key compromise, what is the emergency cadence for notifying Atlas and distribution of a new public key? We need a 4-hour notification SLA for high-severity key compromise.

Procurement: we will expect ShipSafe's updated SLA and a short statement of liabilities for physical transit for our security team.

Regards,
Elena Morales
CISO, AtlasHealth

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: AtlasHealth CISO <ciso@atlashealth.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com, ops@shipsafe.io
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Standalone appliance image revocation and dispatch plan

Elena / Atlas team —

Thanks — answers inline and next actions below.

1) Chain-of-custody pick-up manifest: ShipSafe confirmed they can include GPS coordinates and a signed pickup/delivery record. Marissa, please get an example manifest from ShipSafe that includes timestamped GPS and the two-person signature fields; upload to the Drive link and notify Atlas procurement.

2) Revocation consumption SOP (on-device): we will provide a 2-command flow: 
  a) redwood-verify --manifest /path/to/manifest.json --pubkey /path/to/redwood-pub.pem
  b) redwood-check-revocation --revocation-url <embedded-offline-revocation-file> --manifest /path/to/manifest.json
If the second command returns "REVOKED" the installer must not continue and must contact Redwood on-call. We will provide a minimal shell script and static binary that runs in an isolated environment (sha256 provided). I will add the commands to the Atlas acceptance checklist.

3) Key compromise SLA: Redwood agrees to a 4-hour notification SLA for confirmed private key compromise. In parallel, we will publish an emergency revocation-list and expedite replacement signed bundle. Notification path: email + SMS + DocuSign acknowledgement for chain-of-custody updates.

Evidence package for SOC2: Mina will prepare an evidence ZIP containing: HSM timestamp proofs, signed manifests, build logs (encrypted), ShipSafe scan receipts, and the revocation JSON history. Link (restricted): https://drive.restricted/redwood/atlas/chain-of-custody-20270112

Next actions:
- Marissa: ShipSafe manifest example + updated SLA (due 2027-01-14 17:00 PST)
- Mina: Prepare evidence ZIP and upload to Drive (due 2027-01-14 18:00 PST)
- Karthik: Confirm tooling (redwood-verify + redwood-check-revocation) binaries and provide SHA256 checksums (due 2027-01-15 12:00 PST)

Attachments: signed-keyring-20270110.pem, appliance-image-v3.2.tar.gz.sig, revocation-list-20270112.json

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
